title: Keep workload Nix separate from the appliance system generation
rationale: The image-based Nanoserver appliance does not bake in Nix CLI/daemon or system switching. The intended model is a separately installed Nix workload layer atop the running appliance, similar to installing Nix on a non-NixOS host, with an independent lifecycle and restricted workload-only authority. It may evaluate/apply separate workload outputs, but must never manage the base NixOS generation, boot, /etc, host users/network, or unrelated systemd services. Rootless Podman/Quadlet is the first fit. Determine whether the standard multi-user daemon/store can be safely isolated from the versioned /nix/store and ephemeral root, or whether a stronger boundary is required; do not assume the standard installer is compatible. Libvirt management is privileged: do not grant unrestricted qemu:///system or sudo; require a fixed host-owned activator with explicit domain, path, network, and lifecycle allowlists and no arbitrary shell/hooks. Keep writable VM disks under /persist. Use nix-keys only for trust/bootstrap identity and nix-secrets for runtime-only credentials; never embed secrets in derivations. Workload updates must not alter the booted OS generation. Threat-model and prototype this boundary before host-side installation or deployment.

title: GitOps stages appliance updates into the inactive slot; reboot stays manual
rationale: Desired-state policy: declare the Nanoserver base image version in Git; after CI, publish a new immutable signed release automatically. A component-specific systemd-sysupdate poller stages the signed base image without rebooting. If slot A is running, A remains protected and newer updates replace pending B until the user manually reboots. Keep boot-count health rollback and v2/v3 artifacts. Do not bake Nix CLI/daemon into the base appliance image or use it for system switching; a separately installed, restricted workload Nix layer is tracked by the related workload-runtime decision and must not change the base generation. Current evidence: sysupdate.nix defines daily polling and reboot.enable=false, but the generic systemd-sysupdate.service fails with No transfer definitions found while --component=nanoserver works; appliance-update manually stages and arms a one-shot. Before enabling automation, prove repeated staging targets only inactive B and preserves A, and degraded-mirror/missing-ESP/signature failures stop safely.

title: Automate staging only; retain manual A/B reboot and active-slot rollback
rationale: The appliance remains Nix-free; Git declares the desired image, CI verifies/signs/releases it, and a component-specific systemd-sysupdate reconciler polls and stages it. Do not automatically reboot. When A is running, preserve A and stage a new update into pending B; if a still newer version arrives before reboot, replace B while A stays bootable. The user manually initiates reboot. Keep the one-shot boot target and boot-count health rollback, but verify the actual sysupdate transfer semantics and repeated-stage behavior before enabling the timer: current transfers use ProtectVersion=%A and InstancesMax=2, while the generic service fails due missing default-component transfers. Use the existing A/B and degraded-mirror checks, and fail closed.

title: Software update A/B alternates versions; physical USB slots remain redundant
rationale: A/B in appliance update policy means software versions: active is the running IMAGE_VERSION; staged is a newer version. ProtectVersion=%A and InstancesMax=2 preserve active plus one staged version. Further newer versions replace the pending version; after staged B boots and becomes active, the next update replaces the other (older) software version. Reboot remains user-controlled. This is independent of physical USB/ESP A/B: both mirrored USB boot paths retain their slot-specific UKIs. Do not change physical transfer targets. The automatic service must select --component=nanoserver, call the guarded preflight/stage wrapper, verify artifacts, and arm one-shot without reboot. Publisher and live rollout remain separately authorized.

title: Treat Home Manager removal as a scoped audit, not a blanket migration
rationale: The 2024 article https://ayats.org/blog/no-home-manager raises credible tradeoffs around option overlap, mutable activation, backups, and maintenance surface, but is personal experience rather than proof that HM should be removed. This repo uses HM for substantial user configuration and has integrated plus standalone profiles. Keep the AIO profile disabled pending the platform transition and retain its source. Audit feature-by-feature before migration; consider wrappers or system-owned config where they fit. Search found no active mkOutOfStoreSymlink use; confirm during the audit. Keep appliance workload Nix distinct from dotfile management.

title: Keep K3s clients opt-in until cluster rollout
rationale: Expose k9s and kubectl through the separate opt-in NixOS host feature hosts/features/opt-in/k3s-tools.nix, but do not select it in Nanoserver v4 A/B. The current rollout keeps K3s disabled and adds no kubeconfig, credentials, or cluster access. Activate only under a separately planned and authorized cluster stage, after checking client/server compatibility and access scope.

title: Keep broad direnv trust; disable wildcard SSH agent forwarding
rationale: Retain the `/home/rona/Repositories` direnv whitelist prefix because the workspace has 90+ repositories and per-repository approval is too much friction; keep load_dotenv=false and strict_env=true. Disable agent forwarding for *.local and *.ts.net until a concrete onward-SSH need appears. Leave the options commented as follow-up markers and enable only for exact hosts when justified.
